bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in oatpp::json::Utils::escapeUtf8Char OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=387626404 ``` Crash type: Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 Crash state: oatpp::json::Utils::escapeUtf8Char oatpp::json::Utils::escapeString oatpp::json::Serializer::serializeString ```
bug_description.normalized: During JSON serialization, oatpp estimates escaped UTF-8 output length from the leading-byte sequence length instead of the decoded Unicode code point. For attacker-controlled legacy 5-byte UTF-8 sequences, calcEscapedStringSize() reserves 11 bytes in the `charSize > 4` bucket while escapeUtf8Char() decodes the code point onto the 12-byte surrogate-pair writer path. Repeated one-byte underestimates allocate an undersized heap string, advance the output cursor past the allocation, and a later Hex::writeUInt16 store crosses the end of that string.

source.value_from: The PoC has already been accepted as JSON and materialized into a tree; this statement selects the attacker-controlled string node that is passed into the vulnerable escaping logic.
source.description: Project serializer consumes the attacker-controlled string value that will be escaped into the undersized output buffer.

root_cause.code: result += 11; // '\u+FFFFFFFF' - 11 chars NOT JSON standard case
root_cause.description: The saved PoC is a JSON `s` string containing repeated `0xf8`-prefixed legacy 5-byte UTF-8 sequences such as `f8 c2 2b c2 c2` and `f8 c2 c2 c2 c2`. The estimator uses the UTF-8 byte-sequence length bucket for `charSize > 4` and adds 11 bytes, but those same saved sequences decode to code points that `escapeUtf8Char()` serializes with the 12-byte surrogate-pair path.

sink.description: After repeated one-byte underestimates, `buffer` aliases a position at the end of the heap string; this four-byte hex store for a later escaped character crosses the allocated `escapedSize` boundary, matching the ASAN frame at Utils.cpp:200 and Hex.cpp:41.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC is accepted as JSON and deserialized into a mapping tree rather than rejected before serializer code runs.

fine_trace.note: Project serializer selects the attacker-controlled string node from the parsed tree; this is the concrete byte string later escaped by `Utils::escapeString()`.
The selected string's raw bytes and length are passed to the string escaping routine with the configured UTF-8 escaping flags.
Serializer invokes string escaping with `FLAG_ESCAPE_ALL`, so non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes take the UTF-8 escaping path instead of being copied as-is.

fine_trace.code: result += 11; // '\u+FFFFFFFF' - 11 chars NOT JSON standard case
fine_trace.note: For each saved `0xf8`-prefixed 5-byte sequence in the JSON `s` string, the estimator uses only the leading-byte sequence length and adds 11 bytes.
The underestimated total `escapedSize` is used to allocate the heap-backed result string that will receive escaped output.

`encodeUtf8Char()` decodes those 5-byte PoC sequences into code points below `0x00200000`, so the writer takes the 12-byte surrogate-pair path while the estimator reserved only 11 bytes for each such sequence.
The caller advances `pos` by the 12 bytes written for each such sequence, while the allocation size was computed with 11 bytes for each of them; repeated sequences accumulate a cursor/allocation gap.
The cumulative 1-byte gaps from the repeated 5-byte sequences make the output cursor reach beyond the heap string's `escapedSize`; ASAN reports this later four-byte hex store crossing the buffer end.

format.name: JSON object for oatpp::json::ObjectMapper
format.contract: The saved testcase is a JSON object `{"s":"..."}` whose string value contains repeated `0xf8`-prefixed legacy 5-byte UTF-8 sequences, including `f8 c2 2b c2 c2`, `f8 c2 40 c2 c2`, and `f8 c2 c2 c2 c2`. These bytes make `getUtf8CharSequenceLength(a)` return 5 while `encodeUtf8Char(sequence, length)` yields a code point below `0x00200000`; each such sequence is estimated as 11 bytes but written as 12 bytes, so the cumulative output cursor crosses the allocated escaped string.
